high_severity_items.summary: Federal Reserve Survey of Consumer Finances shows U.S. household debt delinquencies at the highest level since 2010, with the share of families behind on payments jumping to nearly 20% and payment-to-income stress rising, while net worth gains remained concentrated among higher earners. The data points to building consumer credit strain that could weigh on lenders' credit costs and on discretionary household spending, without an imminent systemic trigger.
high_severity_items.title: Americans' debt problems are flashing a warning not seen since the Great Recession

high_severity_items.summary: Record U.S. crude production is not resolving a domestic diesel squeeze: distillate inventories are historically low and expected to stay below the five-year range into 2027, pushing diesel prices to records. The bottleneck appears to be refining/distillate supply rather than crude availability, implying persistent cost pressure on diesel-intensive sectors.
high_severity_items.title: Why Record Crude Output Can’t Solve America’s Diesel Crisis

high_severity_items.summary: Hurricane Isaias has shut in roughly 71.5% of U.S. Gulf of Mexico oil production (~1.46 million bpd) and about 59% of Gulf natural gas output, forcing operator evacuations. This is a concentrated, short-lived physical supply disruption to offshore energy output, raising near-term commodity supply pressure while weighing on affected producers' volumes.
high_severity_items.title: Hurricane Isaias Shuts In 71% of U.S. Gulf Oil Production
